entities.summary:
Pete Seeger was an American singer, songwriter, musician, and left-wing social activist whose life and work had a profound impact on the development of American folk music and the Civil Rights Movement.

Born on May 3, 1919, in New York City, Seeger grew up in a family of activists and was influenced by his father, Charles Seeger, a musicologist, and his mother, Constance Reid Seeger, a composer. He began his music career in the 1940s, performing on nationwide radio and recording hit songs with The Weavers, including "Goodnight, Irene," which topped the charts for 13 weeks in 1950.

In the 1960s, Seeger re-emerged on the public scene as a prominent singer of protest music in support of the Civil Rights Movement. He performed at benefit concerts, participated in peace marches, and used his music to raise awareness about social justice issues. His music and activism were deeply influenced by his Marxist and socialist ideology, which he adopted in the 1940s.

Seeger's legacy extends beyond his own music and activism. He helped to popularize American folk music, paving the way for future generations of musicians. His work also contributed to the development of the Civil Rights Movement, inspiring countless activists and artists to use music and art as a form of social commentary and resistance.

As a symbol of the power of music to inspire social change, Pete Seeger's story is one of enduring relevance and importance. His music and activism continue to inspire new generations of artists and activists, ensuring that his legacy will endure for years to come.
